headline: Democrats' midterm win and Carney's budget reshape the agenda
summary: Democrats won both chambers of the U.S. Congress, capped by Scott Colom's upset Senate win in Mississippi, and Ottawa tabled a budget with a $62.3-billion deficit. Oil slid on hopes of an Iran deal before rebounding, Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large prisoner swap, and Ontario appointed powerful new regional chairs across the GTA.

top.headline: Carney government's second budget projects a $62.3B deficit
top.what: Finance Minister Champagne tabled a budget with a $62.3-billion deficit for 2026-27 and about $142 billion in new spending over five years, including a pledge to end homelessness within a decade.
top.why: It sets federal taxes, spending and borrowing while tariffs and higher interest rates squeeze households.

top.headline: Democrats take Congress; Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat
top.what: Democrats won both chambers on Nov. 3, and on Wednesday Scott Colom was projected the winner in Mississippi as Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith conceded; Alaska's Senate race is the last one uncalled.
top.why: A Democratic Congress can investigate the administration and contest tariffs starting in January.

top.headline: Oil swings as Trump holds off on Iran strikes but keeps blockade
top.what: Brent fell below US$90 on Tuesday for the first time since August on deal hopes, then settled at US$92.76 on Wednesday as Iran said the Strait of Hormuz would never return to its pre-war status.
top.why: Oil prices drive GTA gas prices, inflation and the Bank of Canada's next rate move.

top.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to large prisoner swap at first talks since February
top.what: U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi produced agreement on a large prisoner exchange but no progress on territory or a ceasefire; envoy Witkoff heads to Moscow next.
top.why: Any deal or breakdown shapes European security and Canada's allied commitments.

top.headline: Ontario names eight regional chairs with 'strong chair' powers
top.what: The province appointed the heads of Durham, Halton, Muskoka, Niagara, Peel, Waterloo, York and Simcoe, drawing conflict-of-interest complaints over Steven Del Duca in York.
top.why: Appointed chairs now steer regional budgets that drive property taxes, housing approvals and services.

top.headline: Hegseth impeachment shelved 211-204; Jim Jordan to lead House GOP
top.what: Eleven absent Democrats let Republicans send impeachment articles against the defence secretary to committee, and House Republicans picked Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise as their next leader.
top.why: It previews a combative divided Washington when Democrats take the House in January.

top.headline: Toronto freezes most hiring as it faces a $1.1-billion budget gap
top.what: With Premier Ford ruling out a second 'New Deal', the city paused most hiring to start closing its projected 2027 shortfall.
top.why: Without new money, Toronto residents face pressure on property taxes, TTC fares or services.

top.headline: Canada loses 4,700 jobs in October; unemployment rises to 6.7%
top.what: Statistics Canada says employment slipped slightly in October and the jobless rate rose 0.2 points to 6.7%, its highest since April.
top.why: A softer job market weighs against further Bank of Canada rate hikes on Dec. 9.
